headline: Central Kentucky turns wet Friday while the Upstate stays hot and mainly dry through Friday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Southwest flow keeps Danville and the Bluegrass warm and dry through Thursday. A slow cold front then brings widespread showers and a few thunderstorms Friday, with cooler temperatures and locally heavy rain possible; severe-weather risk appears low.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, warm and dry. Southwest wind stays around 5–10 mph. Skies remain mostly clear tonight, with a milder low in the lower to middle 60s.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No official hazard expected; unseasonable afternoon heat near 90°F
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, hot and increasingly humid with southwest wind around 7–12 mph. Clouds increase Thursday night as a cold front approaches, and scattered showers may begin after midnight.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: Locally heavy rain and isolated thunder; severe-weather risk appears low
days.forecast: Widespread showers and a few thunderstorms are likely as the front crosses the region. Rain and cloud cover should hold temperatures well below Thursday's levels. A general 0.5–1.5 inches is possible across the broader forecast area, with locally higher totals, but the precise rain-band timing remains uncertain.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry and increasingly hot through Thursday, then changes sharply Friday. Plan on a wet Friday with locally heavy rain possible, but current instability and wind profiles do not support a high severe-storm threat. The faster GFS and slower ECMWF solutions create moderate uncertainty in Friday's exact temperature and rain timing.
kentucky.confidence: High through Thursday; moderate on Friday frontal timing and rainfall placement

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Clemson and Central remain sunny, warm and dry through Thursday. Friday turns hotter and somewhat more humid, but the approaching front and its organized rain should remain northwest of the area until Saturday.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny, warm and dry with a light east-southeast wind. Clear skies and nearly calm wind tonight favor a larger Clemson-to-sheltered-valley temperature spread, with the coolest spots falling into the middle 50s.

days.label: Thursday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with light south to southwest wind. Afternoon temperatures reach the middle to upper 80s, followed by a mostly clear night with lows ranging from the upper 50s in cooler pockets to the lower 60s near Clemson.

days.label: Friday
days.precipitation: 10–20% Friday; rising to 30–40% near Saturday dawn
days.hazard: No official hazard expected; shower risk begins increasing near the end of the period
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, hot and increasingly humid. Organized rain should remain to the northwest through Friday, although a stray shower near the mountains cannot be ruled out. Clouds increase Friday night, with shower chances beginning to rise near Saturday dawn at the very end of this forecast window.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate remains dry and summerlike through Friday, with daytime highs in the middle 80s to near 90. The main frontal rain threat arrives Saturday; shower chances only begin to rise near the final hours of this 72-hour period. Low-temperature ranges are intentionally wider to represent the repeatedly cooler KLQK sheltered-site behavior.
upstate.confidence: High through Thursday; moderate-high Friday, with increasing uncertainty near the Saturday boundary

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts for Danville and Clemson were generated at approximately 7:34 AM EDT. Official airport observations span 6:55–7:15 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:54 AM and 6:47 AM EDT, respectively. Louisville supports widespread Friday rain, low severe-weather potential and a broader 0.5–1.5-inch rainfall range, while noting faster GFS and slower ECMWF timing. Greenville-Spartanburg supports dry weather through Thursday, Friday heat and the primary frontal rain threat arriving over the weekend.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the approximately 7:34 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

Model inventories checked at 7:35 AM EDT showed the 10Z HRRR complete through forecast hour 18, the 10Z RAP through hour 21, 06Z NAM through hour 84, NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 384, and the 06Z GEFS mean through hour 252. The latest complete ECMWF deterministic cycle available at that check was 00Z through hour 360.

College of DuPage NEXLAB model panels were inspected directly and their run and valid times were preserved. Live Southeast radar and visible-satellite links were also consulted for situational context; no unsupported pixel-level claim is made from those continuously updating products.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

Verification feedback through 2026-09-29 was consulted before setting ranges. Central Kentucky overnight ranges were shifted about 1–2°F lower where the KDVK signal applies; Upstate high ranges were tempered about 1°F and overnight ranges widened downward to represent KLQK's recurring cold bias. Very-low precipitation wording was also avoided where residual uncertainty exists because the historical 0–20% bin has verified wetter than forecast.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted nighttime ranges about 1–2°F lower where the KDVK low-temperature signal is relevant. Kept daytime ranges centered on current guidance because KDVK high bias remains below the correction threshold and KLEX does not share it.

Tempered the KCEU-side daytime ceiling by about 1°F and widened nighttime ranges downward to include the recurring KLQK cold-pocket behavior. The full -4°F KLQK correction was not applied region-wide because it is station-specific.

Avoided overconfident 5%-or-less precipitation wording because the verified 0–20% probability bin has observed rain more often than forecast; retained higher probabilities where official guidance supports the Friday Kentucky event.
